scope: Read-only patient/consent/support content challenge of external batch5 v0.84.64 draft; no app, source-rule, candidate, commit or push changes.
clinical_rule_freeze: Not asserted; parent has paused v64 work while applying v62.
limits: Retained current NCCP and product-source packet reviewed; no new exhaustive source campaign.
This is a content review, not rendered consent/PDF/browser approval or clinical prescribing approval.
The clinician efficacy KB was snapshotted for reproducibility, but quantitative efficacy and decision-engine rules were outside this focused review.

findings.location: support[title=Acute irinotecan reactions].text and inherited phase support
findings.observed: Atropine is prescribed where appropriate; glaucoma requires review.
findings.source_requirement: Both current NCCP documents explicitly state atropine should not be used in patients with glaucoma.
findings.correction: State the exclusion explicitly, e.g. Tell the team if you have glaucoma: the national regimen says atropine should not be used in patients with glaucoma. Keep dose selection owned by the clinical team.

findings.observed: Mesna bars start=1,end=2, despite the second 24-hour infusion starting with day-2 ifosfamide.
findings.source_requirement: 900 mg/m² pre-ifosfamide and 3000 mg/m² over 24 hours starting with ifosfamide on each of days 1 and 2. The final continuous infusion therefore extends into day 3 by actual clock.
findings.correction: Show continuation into day 3 with wording that it completes the day-2 24-hour infusion; do not imply a third day-3 starting dose. Recheck day-3 recovery/support text.

findings.observed: Baseline and before each cycle, followed by conditional additional tests during or after treatment when guidance, symptoms or abnormalities indicate them.
findings.source_requirement: Current Temodal product information states liver tests should be checked after each treatment cycle for all patients; delayed liver toxicity may occur weeks or more after the last treatment.
findings.correction: Explicitly include after-each-cycle liver tests, including the final cycle, while preserving the current pre-cycle national checks and additional clinically indicated checks. Do not transfer the separate 42-day glioma mid-cycle instruction.

findings.observed: The dedicated acute-atropine card and temozolomide capsule instructions are removed and the explicit day-8 vincristine-only note is present. However, a remaining combined bowel paragraph still describes acute infusion cholinergic symptoms and prescribed atropine.
findings.correction: For the day-8 phase, retain delayed diarrhoea, urgent warning signs and the ongoing infection/constipation plan; trim the acute-irinotecan paragraph to avoid implying an irinotecan premedication or administration on day 8. Retain the full explanation on the overall regimen/combination phase.

findings.observed: Do not alter infusion or mesna-pump settings yourself.
findings.correction: Remove mesna-pump from these two regimens because neither includes mesna; retain suitable line/infusion and temozolomide-handling advice.

findings.observed: Irinotecan 50 mg/m² intravenously and temozolomide 125 mg/m² in cycle 1; only the treating team may select 150 mg/m² from cycle 2 after reviewing toxicity by mouth are given on days 1–5 of each 21-day cycle.
findings.correction: Use separate sentences for intravenous irinotecan 50 mg/m² on days 1–5 and oral temozolomide 125 mg/m² on days 1–5 in cycle 1. Then state only the treating team may select 150 mg/m² from cycle 2 after toxicity review. This avoids attaching by-mouth ambiguously after the escalation clause.

findings.observed: Final VC, with dactinomycin optional and no doxorubicin, is independently labelled high.
findings.source_requirement: The current source explicitly labels the IE and VAC portions overall high, lists etoposide low, ifosfamide moderate, vincristine minimal and doxorubicin/cyclophosphamide high. It does not separately classify final doxorubicin-free VC or optional dactinomycin in this section.
findings.correction: Do not silently downgrade the source overall prevention plan. Clarify whether high is intended as the overall source regimen policy or obtain a pharmacy/local classification for the exact final selected agents before presenting it as a separately source-verified phase class.

confirmed_checks.result: All five include the complete generic paragraph plus every selected agent. Named risks and urgent watch text exactly match the retained agent definitions; source IDs are intentionally normalized to profile nccp/product IDs. Includes serious infection, bleeding, bowel effects, fertility/pregnancy, lasting injury, later cancers, death, nails, sexual wellbeing and thrombosis.

00675/00747 agent display name, mechanism explanation, schedule summary and final phase timeline make dactinomycin optional for cycles 12 and 14. No doxorubicin is stated in those final even administrations. Future generated consent must respect the actual consultant-selected option, not infer selection from inclusion in the full phase agents array.

00504 and 00757 explicitly require prevention, supported by their NCCP sources; 00754 says consider individually, without turning this into a universal requirement. Antifungal consideration and azole-vincristine interaction remain visible.

00757 explicitly guards adult portal scope against automatic paediatric extension; 00675 retains adolescent/young-adult 14-day context and 00747 adult 21-day context without invented numeric cutoffs. No adult fixed-dose loperamide schedule was found in the patient instructions. 00504 does not invent a fixed atropine dose; 00757 names its source 250 micrograms as a team-confirmed prescription.
Current 00504 and 00757 combination phase risk is moderate-to-high, agreeing with source temozolomide moderate-to-high and irinotecan moderate; day-8 vincristine phase is minimal.

All three cycle blocks remain high because ifosfamide remains present; current NCCP lists ifosfamide high, doxorubicin moderate, dactinomycin moderate and vincristine minimal. Later omission of doxorubicin is explicit.

Cyclophosphamide cites the current January 2026 Irish Seacross product. Dactinomycin is labelled as current UK manufacturer information with supplied Irish product reconciliation; the old Irish withdrawn licence is not presented as current authorisation. Unlicensed indication discussion remains explicit for 00504/00757.

Dactinomycin liver small-vessel obstruction/radiation recall/extravasation, cyclophosphamide bladder/kidney/cardiopulmonary/late risks, ifosfamide brain/kidney toxicity despite mesna, vincristine severe bowel/peripheral-nerve toxicity, irinotecan early versus delayed bowel toxicity, and temozolomide prolonged marrow/liver/opportunistic-infection risks remain present.

Dedicated acute atropine card and capsule administration/missed-dose text are absent from current vin8 support. Delayed diarrhoea and ongoing prevention remain. One combined paragraph still needs trimming, recorded in B5-C04.
